title: Pouding Chômeur: Québec Pudding Cake Baked in Maple Cream Sauce
summary: A simple butter cake baked under hot maple syrup and cream, which sinks to become a thick sauce beneath a golden crust.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Set the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) with a shelf in the upper third.

steps.title: Warm the sauce
steps.text: Heat the maple syrup, cream and salt in the saucepan over medium heat for about 5 min, until just simmering. Whisk and pour into the heatproof jug.

steps.title: Combine the dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Whisk the milk, eggs and vanilla in the other bowl, add to the dry ingredients and whisk smooth, then whisk in the melted butter until glossy.

steps.title: Pour on the sauce
steps.text: Spread the batter in the baking dish set on the tray. Pour the hot sauce slowly into one corner so it floats across the batter rather than digging holes in it. The tray catches any bubbling over.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 30-35 min until deep golden and a skewer pushed into the cake part comes out clean. As it bakes, the lighter batter rises up through the denser sauce, which settles at the bottom.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Leave it for 10 min so the sauce thickens, then spoon portions onto plates and flip each over so the sauce sits on top.

tips: Use pure maple syrup, not a flavoured syrup, or the sauce will be thin and one-dimensional.
A common mistake is pouring the sauce fast in the middle; pour gently into a corner.
Serve warm with a spoonful of crème fraîche or plain yoghurt to cut the sweetness.
Dark maple syrup gives the deepest flavour.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat portions in the microwave or a 180 °C (160 °C fan) oven until piping hot.
